name: Question 9
worked_solution:
To find ${g}_{xy}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{x}(x,y)$ with respect to $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({g}_{x}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{x+2y}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{(x+2y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

To find ${g}_{yx}(x,y)$ we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative ${g}_{y}(x,y)$ with respect to $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{yx}(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({g}_{y}(x,y)) \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{2}{x+2y}) \\  & =-\frac{2}{(x+2y)^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Next, we evaluate ${g}_{xy}(x,y)$ and ${g}_{yx}(x,y)$ at $(-1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{xy}(-1,2) & =-\frac{2}{((-1)+2(2))^{2}}=-\frac{2}{9} \\ {g}_{yx}(-1,2) & =-\frac{2}{((-1)+2(2))^{2}}=-\frac{2}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we have

$$
{g}_{xy}(-1,2)+{g}_{yx}(-1,2)=-\frac{4}{9}.
$$

Question 9

Find gxy(x,y)+gyx(x,y) at (−1,2) given that gx(x,y)=1x+2y and gy(x,y)=2x+2y.

a
9
b
−29
c
−1
d
−49
e
−19
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find gxy(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative gx(x,y) with respect to y:

gxy(x,y)=∂∂y(gx(x,y))=∂∂y(1x+2y)=−2(x+2y)2

To find gyx(x,y) we differentiate the given first-order partial derivative gy(x,y) with respect to x:

gyx(x,y)=∂∂x(gy(x,y))=∂∂x(2x+2y)=−2(x+2y)2

Next, we evaluate gxy(x,y) and gyx(x,y) at (−1,2): gxy(−1,2)=−2((−1)+2(2))2=−29gyx(−1,2)=−2((−1)+2(2))2=−29

Finally, we have

gxy(−1,2)+gyx(−1,2)=−49.
